elements.element: The licence extends to Customer's affiliates.
elements.evidence: Inserted clause: "Affiliates. Upon written notice to Commerce One, the licenses granted to Corio under this Section 2 shall extend to Corio's affiliates." Corio is defined as the named entity only, so the affiliate extension is additive and not duplicative.

elements.element: The licence extends to contractors acting on Customer's behalf.
elements.evidence: Neither Section 2.1/2.2 nor the inserted clause mentions contractors or subcontractors acting on Corio's behalf; the grants run to Corio (and now affiliates) only. To meet this the drafter would need to add "and contractors acting on Corio's behalf" to the Section 2 grant.
Section 2.2: "royalty-free, fully paid up, perpetual right and license in the Territory".

Section 2.2 (the fully paid-up licence) says "royalty-free, fully paid up, perpetual" but omits "irrevocable"; only Section 2.1, the fee-bearing licence, is expressly "perpetual and irrevocable". The word "irrevocable" must be added to the Section 2.2 grant.

elements.element: A subscription licence is terminable only for uncured material breach.
elements.evidence: Conditional element whose condition does not apply: the Section 2 grants are fee-bearing perpetual/irrevocable (2.1) and fully paid-up perpetual (2.2); no subscription-term licence is granted, so there is no subscription grant requiring a breach-only termination limit.

elements.element: The licence is transferable to Customer's successors.
elements.evidence: Sections 2.1 and 2.2 are "nontransferable (except in accordance with Section 14.1)", and Section 14.1 permits assignment "in connection with the merger or acquisition of such party or the sale of all or substantially all of its assets related to this Agreement without such consent" and binds "successors and permitted assigns"; the direct-competitor consent carve-out is a minor shortfall only.

elements.element: Customer's affiliates are covered on written notice.
elements.evidence: Inserted clause expressly conditions the extension on notice: "Upon written notice to Commerce One, the licenses granted to Corio under this Section 2 shall extend to Corio's affiliates."

elements.element: The licence is transferable to a successor in a merger or acquisition transaction.
elements.evidence: Retained Section 14.1: "either party shall have the right to assign this Agreement in connection with the merger or acquisition of such party or the sale of all or substantially all of its assets related to this Agreement without such consent", and the Section 2 grants are transferable in accordance with Section 14.1.

reasons: Fallback checklist is complete: the single inserted sentence supplies affiliate coverage on written notice, and successor transfer on an M&A or substantially-all-assets sale already exists in retained Section 14.1 (via the Section 2 "except in accordance with Section 14.1" carve-out). The finding is therefore position-complete at the fallback level.

Preferred level fails on two elements: (a) no grant to contractors acting on Corio's behalf anywhere in Section 2, and (b) the fully paid-up Section 2.2 licence is perpetual but not stated to be irrevocable. If the preferred position were pursued, add "and contractors acting on its behalf" to the Section 2 grants and insert "irrevocable" into Section 2.2.

Minimal: exactly one concise insertion tracking the fallback element; no favourable retained language (perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free, Section 14.1 transfer right, Section 2.10 territorial expansion) was deleted or paraphrased, and no extras such as survival tails, flow-down obligations, or affiliate liability language were added. "Corio" is the named entity and does not already include affiliates, so there is no duplicate coverage.

Preserves intent: the new sentence sits alongside Section 2 without contradicting the Territory limit, the nontransferability qualifier, or the revenue-sharing and fee mechanics; no undefined term or dangling cross-reference is created ("affiliates" is undefined in the Agreement but used in its ordinary sense - consider defining "Affiliate" if Commerce One pushes back on scope).
Classification of "deviation" is correct as of the original text: affiliate coverage was absent with no mechanism to add it, which is a material failure of the fallback.
